scope: Actual WITHOUT ROWID primary-key reseek at pending-row visit and after BEFORE programs. Same-PK reinsertion is visited and different-PK rekeying is skipped, with original SET/OLD registers and actual current unassigned fields. Finite native comparisons, not complete triggered SQL equivalence.

negative_results.stage: Published directed-key checkpoint; unseeded diagnostic baseline
negative_results.reason: A private ordinal missed a deleted/reinserted same-PK row, or incorrectly found a row moved to another declared PK. Later-row replacement controls passed when the ordinal happened to be reused. Final harnesses separate API/file metrics and use fresh seeded key strings and RHS increments.

implementation: RowStep stores the actual declared primary values selected at statement entry, in addition to the private point locator. Ordinary rowid-table behavior remains unchanged.

CoreWithoutRowidTable.findPrimary extracts the real source-derived PK tuple and compares it with the current table using actual declared collations. It never equates SQL rows through the private ordinal.

Before visiting a pending row, and again after BEFORE programs, the actual PK is looked up in current state. Deleted/reinserted same-PK rows are found; rows moved to a different PK are skipped. The actual new private locator is passed to replacement preparation.

Only the private point condition is rebound. SET expressions already frozen before BEFORE, original OLD/NEW register images and actual current unassigned fields retain their existing execution paths. Actual direct/total change counts reflect whether the outer point was reached.

The maintained new group verifies a BEFORE deletion/reinsertion keeps replacement unassigned fields, writes the original frozen RHS and accounts body plus direct changes. C and storage record formats are unchanged.

evaluation_protocols.public_file_modes: 7868 public file comparisons, including 12 new real-PK-reseek cases across rollback and WAL modes. Final new keys/RHS increments are independently seeded from the unseeded diagnostic baseline.
evaluation_protocols.same_connection: 354 continuing API cases, including six new reseek cases, use actual continuation after errors and native stdout/change-register observations. These are separate from public file cases.
evaluation_protocols.crashes: All existing 516 finite SIGKILL samples are rerun on this final runtime; no additional crash schedule/category is claimed by this semantic change.
evaluation_protocols.named_features: The original finite named survey remains 88/88; not a global coverage percentage.

proof_scope: The full build, 414 maintained Lean groups and required audits pass. The new algorithmic regression checks the actual source-aware row pipeline, frozen RHS, retained replacement fields and counters. Existing checked-image/applied-write/recovery contracts remain compiled. No global triggered-SQL or primary-reseek equivalence theorem is claimed.
limitations: Non-ABORT declaration policies, inline primary direction syntax, UTF-16 WITHOUT ROWID acquisition/writes, auxiliary foreign-parent/planner admission, recursive auxiliary REPLACE with DELETE programs, ALTER/UPSERT and wider expression/phase combinations remain work.

Covering scan admission is limited to the stated simple full-coverage shape and field-count criterion; arbitrary WHERE/order/distinct/group shapes, planner costs/statistics and wider native planner choices are not claimed.
Bulk physical root-page layout is not globally SQLite-identical; pending new-object schema metadata and larger root-preservation cases remain separate work.
Wider error codes/phases, FAIL/IGNORE/ROLLBACK controls, triggered UPSERT, INSTEAD OF/temp triggers, writable CTEs, trigger-aware ALTER and deferred private-function declarations remain work.

UTF-16 writes/setters, native-key/materialization limits, pending new physical allocations and earlier SQL/storage limitations remain. The finite process-kill samples do not establish every syscall/power-loss schedule.
